messages:
Jordan (docs): Quick sync — I want to split the current metering/headers doc into a 'Metering API v1 (legacy)' and 'Metering API v2' section. V2 will rename some headers and add a field for effective_tier. Need: 1) short migration blurb, 2) Python + Go SDK snippets showing new header usage, 3) a short note for the pricing table about tier fall-through and burst credits. Any objections or hidden gotchas?
Alex Chen: Sounds good. Is the change purely header rename (X-Redwood-Usage -> X-Redwood-Metering) or are we changing semantics for how we compute buckets?
Jordan (docs): Mostly header rename + we surface effective_tier in exports for analytics. Billing semantics unchanged, but there are two corner cases: switching between ratecards mid-month (backfill behavior) and small bursts that should be covered by burst credits — both should be documented.
Mira Patel: Can we include a compact curl example for the docs TOC? People still search for curl first. Also who owns the dashboard panel link — I need to update the 'tier visualization' link in the page.
Samir Rao: I'll file the panel link PR once you confirm the panel id. Quick note: when customers flip to v2 we don't retroactively recalc prior events, we tag future events with effective_tier. Add an explicit line: "events prior to the switch remain on legacy_tier". :thumbsup:
Vera (data-analytics): Please add the export column name exactly: "effective_tier" and mention it may be null for legacy rows. Also add a sample export row so analysts know what to expect. Example row (for the docs):
```
{"timestamp":"2026-02-12T14:23:01Z","customer_id":"acct_123","usage_units":1200,"rate_card":"starter","effective_tier":"starter_plus","metering_key":"embed.requests"}
```
Jordan (docs): Perfect — that JSON snippet is exactly the kind of thing we need. Will add caveat about nulls.
Alex Chen: For SDK snippets, I'd prefer we show both header approach and SDK client header setter. Draft Python snippet:
```python
# Python SDK example (pseudo)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
cli = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
resp = cli.generate(
  model="open-llama-3",
  prompt="Summarize...",
  headers={"X-Redwood-Metering":"usage_id=abc123;tier=starter_plus"}
)
print(resp.text)
```
And a tiny curl example:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Metering: usage_id=abc123;tier=starter_plus" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Mira Patel: Can we also include a Go snippet? A lot of infra folks ask for it. Keep it short.
Samir Rao: Here's a 4-line Go example you can put inline: `client.SetHeader("X-Redwood-Metering", "usage_id=abc123;tier=starter_plus") // net/http or SDK wrapper`
Jordan (docs): I'll add all three snippets. One docs style question: should we call the header "X-Redwood-Metering" or "Redwood-Metering" (no X-)? My vote: keep X- for backwards compat hints but note we accept both. Thoughts?
Alex Chen: Keep X- for the header in examples (historical pattern). Add note: "Both Redwood-Metering and X-Redwood-Metering are accepted; X- form recommended in examples for clarity."
Vera (data-analytics): Also add a short section in the exports page about how "effective_tier" maps to pricing tiers used in costing dashboards. Analysts will want the exact mapping table. I can draft that if you want.
Jordan (docs): Yes please — if you can drop the mapping table into an MD snippet (just the CSV lines) that would be ideal.
Vera (data-analytics): I can do that today. CSV lines example: `customer_id,rate_card,effective_tier,cost_per_unit` then a couple example rows.
Samir Rao: One more edge: burst credits. We should show a tiny example of how burst credits apply to an overage event and link to the pricing page. Suggest wording: "Burst credits cover transient spikes up to X units in a rolling window; see ratecard table for exact values."
Jordan (docs): Good. I'll draft the burst explanation with a small timeline ascii diagram.
Jordan (docs): Action items: 1) I will open a docs PR with the new Metering v2 section + Python/Go/curl snippets + note on header aliases. 2) Vera to add mapping CSV and sample export rows. 3) Samir to update dashboard panel link and add burst-credit blurb to pricing page. 4) Alex to sanity-check SDK examples (esp. header formatting).
Alex Chen: I'll review the SDK snippets tonight.
deploy-bot: PR created: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4824> — branch: docs/metering-v2-snippets :rocket:
Jordan (docs): Thanks! I'll tag reviewers and link this thread into the PR description. Final ask: keep the migration blurb under 3 bullets so it's easy to scan. :eyes:
